article.Citation/Title: Nicholas, C. R., Wang, J. B., Coker, A., Mitchell, J. M., Klaire, S. S., Yazar-Klosinski, B., Emerson, A., Brown, R. T., & Doblin, R. (2022). The effects of MDMA-assisted therapy on alcohol and substance use in a phase 3 trial for treatment of severe PTSD. Drug and Alcohol Dependence, 233, 109356.
article.InterventionDescription: MDMA, divided oral dose (80+40mg escalating to 120+60mg), 3 experimental 8-hour sessions each flanked by preparatory/integration therapy, clinical trial site setting.

article.Citation/Title: This article is a secondary/exploratory analysis of alcohol and substance-use outcomes drawn from the MAPS-sponsored Phase 3 MDMA-AT trial for severe PTSD. The parent trial, whose primary endpoint was CAPS-5 PTSD severity (not alcohol/substance use), is Mitchell, J.M. et al. (2021), 'MDMA-assisted therapy for severe PTSD: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study,' Nat. Med. 27(6), 1025-1033, cited throughout Methods (§2.1) as the source of full study methods/protocol.
article.Outcome: No outcome is explicitly labeled 'primary' anywhere in the article; both AUDIT (alcohol) and DUDIT (drug) change scores are examined. Per the abstract-leads precedence rule, AUDIT is treated as this article's primary SUD outcome because the Abstract Results paragraph and §3.2 both lead with the AUDIT group difference before mentioning DUDIT, and AUDIT is the only one of the two that reached statistical significance. Value taken as the directly reported Hedges' g=.45 for the MDMA-AT vs Placebo+Therapy AUDIT change-score comparison (Abstract; Results §3.2).
article.SD: Paired with the Outcome value: the F-test reported alongside Hedge's g=.45 for the same AUDIT group difference, printed as 'F(80, 1)=4.20' in both the Abstract and Results §3.2. Reported exactly as printed (df order appears reversed from the conventional F(df_effect, df_error) form) rather than corrected, per the instruction not to construct a decoding theory for a number that looks off.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: N=82 (42 MDMA-AT, 40 Placebo+Therapy) is the number of participants with complete baseline and study-termination AUDIT/DUDIT data used in the reported AUDIT group comparison (§3.1: 'leaving a total of 82 participants that completed both baseline and study termination assessments...Participants with complete data were used in the present analysis').

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: 12 of 14 criteria met. sample_size_power=N: no a priori sample-size or power calculation is reported anywhere in this article; the Discussion only offers a post hoc, informal statement that the narrow AUDIT score distribution 'limited the potential to detect a statistically significant measurable change,' which is not a described power analysis. harms=N: this article contains no dedicated adverse-event/harms/safety section, table, or count; safety data for the parent trial were published separately in Mitchell et al. (2021). n_met=12 < 13, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.

article.Retention (%): 82/90x100=91.11%, using randomized N (90) as the denominator since only a single randomized-N figure is given (§3.1: '90 participants were randomized'). Note: the article states 3 MDMA and 4 Placebo participants withdrew (7 total), which arithmetically implies 83 completers (90-7=83), but the article explicitly states 82 participants completed both assessments. This is an internal numeric inconsistency in the source text; the printed completer count (82) was used as given rather than resolved by inference, per the instruction to report inconsistent numbers as printed and flag them.
article.BaseStatus: Coded '.' as a judgment call. The analyzed sample had 0 current alcohol use disorder in both arms per the MINI (Table 1); only a minority (21/82, 25.6%) had past AUD in remission, and mean baseline AUDIT was subclinical (3.56/40 possible, Table 1). The Discussion states explicitly that 'no participant with even mild AUD was recruited into the study, despite being permitted.' This population does not cleanly map to Severe/Moderate/Mild AUD severity at baseline, so '.' was used rather than guessing a band.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: 'Both' — the parent trial (and this analysis's sample) was conducted across 15 sites in the US, Canada, and Israel (§2.1).
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: 19.75% = sum of non-White race categories in Table 1 (American Indian/Alaska Native 3.70% + Asian 6.17% + Black or African American 2.47% + More than one race 7.41%), consistent with 100% - White 80.25% = 19.75%.
article.PercentFem: 64.63% per Table 1 (Female 53/82); the Abstract/§3.1 text rounds this to 64.6%.
article.Power: Coded 1 (discussed informally, not a priori calculated). No formal power calculation is reported anywhere in the article, but the Discussion states the narrow AUDIT score distribution 'limited the potential to detect a statistically significant measurable change from baseline,' which is treated as a bare discussion of the study being underpowered for this purpose, per the rule that a bare underpowered statement counts as Power=1.
article.SafetyReported: Coded 'N'. This article has no dedicated adverse-event/safety section, table, or AE counts anywhere in the text. The only safety-adjacent statement is that MDMA-AT 'did not demonstrate increased risk of substance use, abuse, or dependence, or increased MDMA use during and 2 months following treatment' (Discussion) — this is a substance-use-risk finding of this analysis, not a general harms/AE assessment. Full safety data for the parent trial were reported separately in Mitchell et al. (2021), which this article does not reproduce.
article.HarmsAssessed: Coded 0 to satisfy the required concordance with SafetyReported='N' (SafetyReported='N' iff HarmsAssessed in {0,3,'.'}).
article.AnyAEReported: 'NA' because SafetyReported='N' per the three-state AE presence table (article silent on AEs/safety entirely).
article.AE_denominator: Coded '.' rather than 'NA' per the explicit rule that AE_denominator is never 'NA'; use '.' when no safety assessment was reported (SafetyReported='N').
article.ArmScope: 'NA' because SafetyReported='N' and there is no AE data to scope to an arm.
article.WorstSeverity: 'NA' because SafetyReported='N', per the three-state AE presence table.
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: Coded 0. The only functioning-adjacent instrument used is the modified Sheehan Disability Scale (SDS), which measures functional impairment/disability in work, social, and family life, not an explicit quality-of-life construct. No other QoL instrument is reported.
article.Followup in months: Coded '.'. The article does not state a precise numeric interval between end of treatment and the 'study termination' AUDIT/DUDIT assessment point. The Discussion's phrase 'did not demonstrate increased risk...during and 2 months following treatment' describes the observation window for a safety-adjacent substance-use-risk claim, not an explicitly stated follow-up duration tied to the AUDIT/DUDIT primary comparison, so it was not used to avoid asserting an unstated number.
article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 1, based on the unadjusted, statistically significant AUDIT group difference favoring MDMA-AT (Hedge's g=.45, F(80,1)=4.20, p=.0436; §3.2). Flagging that this effect was no longer statistically significant after adjusting for baseline AUDIT (p=.52), and that DUDIT (drug use) showed no significant group difference at any timepoint — this is a qualified/partial positive result on the article's own primary (AUDIT) outcome.
article.InterventionTherapy: Coded 1: each of the 3 MDMA/placebo dosing sessions was preceded by 3 90-minute preparatory therapy sessions and followed by 3 90-minute integration therapy sessions (§2.3), i.e., structured therapy well beyond drug administration alone.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0. Participants underwent extensive clinical screening (CAPS-5 threshold ≥35, MINI-assessed psychiatric/SUD exclusions, exclusion of any current SUD other than mild/early-remission-moderate alcohol or cannabis use disorder) typical of a highly screened trial-eligible volunteer sample rather than a real-world clinical or community population.

config_proposal.note: Authors directly report Hedge's g=.45 for the AUDIT (alcohol) change-score group difference, MDMA-AT vs Placebo+Therapy (Abstract; §3.2); this is a direct pass-through of an author-computed Hedges' g requiring no conversion, and the reported positive value already favors MDMA-AT (greater alcohol-use reduction), so direction=1.
